- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., > 0.17 negative values in recent days), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day average), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent high, then apply mean reversion toward 30-day moving average.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., >0.17 for 3+ consecutive days), model frequently overreacts; apply downward bias of 3–7% to prevent overconfidence.
- Model underestimates prices when sentiment is weak or mixed (e.g., sentiment < 0.06 for 3+ days); increase forecast by 1–4% to account for hidden volatility or policy lag.
- Forecast horizon 30d often exhibits lag: true price drops 2–4 days after model’s peak; adjust forecast to align with 2–3 day lag in price decline.
- When sentiment is volatile (e.g., alternating +/– 0.17), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast using 5-day moving average or reduce volatility coefficient by 30%.
